To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy consumption of an electric vehicle can be modeled using an energy graph, that the optimal energy-efficient path in the presence of a limited battery capacity can be computed in O(n), and that acceleration and decelaration costs can be taken into consideration by an unfolding of the energy graph.

the optimal route for an EV is not necessarily the shortest one and that it can be found in O(n) by a generalization of a general shortest-path algorithm using an energy graph and respecting the given constraints.
the energy consumption can be minimized by using the proposed algorithm and that the energy consumption is minimized by using the optimal algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a navigation system for energy-optimized routing of battery powered vehicles.
the development of a novel routing paradigm that is suitable for battery-powered vehicles and that can be integrated into existing routing systems.
the problem of finding the energy-efficient route for a battery-powered electric vehicle in the presence of a given network of recharging stations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed algorithms can be used for energy-efficient routing in real-time and that the algorithms can be used in combination with the proposed unfolding technique to take into account acceleration and decelerations costs for segments with a different cruising speed.
the proposed algorithms and the prototypic navigation application are promising and that further investigations are necessary.
energy-efficient routing is a challenging and interesting problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how the problem of energy-efficient routing can be formulated as a constrained shortest path problem and how it can be solved efficiently.
we have presented an approach for the computation of energy-efficient routes for EVs.
the proposed algorithms can be used for energy-efficient routing in a real-time environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
energy-efficient routing can be achieved by adapting existing shortest path algorithms to the specific requirements of electric vehicles, which is demonstrated with the proposed energy graphs.
the optimal routing problem for battery-powered vehicles is not a hard problem and that the proposed algorithms can be implemented in an efficient manner.
the optimal routing problem for EVs is a CSP with hard and soft (i.e., non-binding) constraints, and that it can be addressed with an adaption of general shortest path algorithms.
